top_signal.title: What takes way too long in your business?
top_signal.summary: I'm looking for real-world problems in the IT and business industry, from small businesses to large enterprises, that are unnecessarily manual, inefficient, slow, or complicated. One example I've encountered is application requests, where an employee submits a helpdesk ticket and then waits for IT to manually review, approve, install, configure, and close the request, even though much of the process could potentially be standardized or automated. However, I'm not only interested in automation — I'm also interested in problems involving poor workflows, disconnected systems, repetitive data entry, communication gaps, reporting, onboarding, procurement, inventory, access management, customer service, or other areas where companies lose significant time or resources. What is something your company makes you do regularly that makes you think, "There has to be a better way to do this"? I'm especially interested in problems that happen frequently and become increasingly painful as a company grows, so I'd appreciate       submitted by     /u/Ashule111       [link]       [comments]
